name: Helix 02
summary: Helix 02 extends Figure's VLA from upper-body control to the whole robot by adding System 0, a 10-million-parameter network running at 1 kHz that handles balance and coordination and was trained on over a thousand hours of human motion capture. Figure reports it replaces 109,504 lines of hand-engineered C++ with a single learned prior. It sits under System 1, a 200 Hz visuomotor policy that now maps every onboard sensor — vision, touch and proprioception — to every actuator, and System 2, the semantic reasoning layer. The demonstration is a four-minute autonomous dishwasher load-and-unload across a full-sized kitchen: 61 sequential loco-manipulation actions with no resets and no human intervention. An April 2026 update added perception-conditioned whole-body control, letting the robot handle stairs, ramps and uneven terrain from RGB alone.
innovation: A learned low-level whole-body controller at 1 kHz, displacing the model-predictive control stack humanoids normally depend on.
Whole-body sensor fusion into one visuomotor policy, including touch and proprioception rather than vision alone.
matters: The strongest public evidence that the classical control layer beneath a humanoid can itself be learned, which is where most hand-engineering in the field still lives.
limits: Company blog only — no paper, no metrics beyond the single demonstration, no independent reproduction.
A curated four-minute run says little about the failure rate across a working day.
lineage: Helix's System 1/System 2 split extended downward with a learned System 0 motion prior.
